principles: Activity logging may recognize runtime-managed roots without expanding canonical project config semantics.
Canonical lattice.config.json parsing must remain schema-stable and backward compatible.
Codex verify should prove the same user-visible heartbeat path that failed in solver-visible.
drivers: global-thin managed projects can be valid adapter roots with only .lattice/lattice.json
writeLog currently skips all roots without canonical project config
runHeartbeat validates by reading the session record from .lattice/activity.jsonl

options.name: A: Add .lattice/lattice.json to PROJECT_CONFIG_FILENAMES
pros: Existing hasProjectConfigFile callers would see global-thin roots
cons: Would make loadConfig try to parse a different schema as canonical project config

options.name: B: Add an explicit runtime activity-root helper
pros: Limits .lattice/lattice.json recognition to activity logging/root detection
Matches the observed failure path directly
cons: Requires replacing specific hasProjectConfigFile checks where activity logging needs runtime-root semantics

options.name: C: Special-case Codex heartbeat to create activity logs directly
pros: Could fix the single failing verify check
cons: Bypasses the shared CLI activity logging path
Leaves session_brief global-fallback behavior inconsistent for other activity readers

chosen: B: Add an explicit runtime activity-root helper
rationale: The bug is in runtime activity-root detection, not canonical config loading. Option B fixes the missing heartbeat while keeping loadConfig scoped to lattice.config.json and avoiding schema confusion.

preMortem.scenario: The helper accepts any .lattice/lattice.json and treats arbitrary directories as Proofbound roots.
preMortem.trigger: Detection only checks file existence instead of assetMode global-thin.
preMortem.consequence: Read-only commands could create .lattice/activity.jsonl in unrelated directories.
preMortem.mitigation: Parse JSON defensively and require assetMode exactly global-thin; add an adversarial regression for non-global-thin metadata.

preMortem.scenario: DONE worktree cleanup fallback regresses because writeLog no longer uses canonical project config checks for main fallback.
preMortem.consequence: Post-DONE logging could recreate ghost worktree directories or pick the wrong root.
preMortem.mitigation: Use the activity-root helper only where logging root eligibility is intended, preserving the durable fallback order and canonical checks where appropriate.

preMortem.scenario: The smoke passes via direct runCodexAdapterChecks but the real installed lattice command still fails.
preMortem.trigger: Tests avoid executing the child process heartbeat path or use a root with lattice.config.json.
preMortem.consequence: solver-visible remains broken despite green local tests.
preMortem.mitigation: Add a managed global-thin-only heartbeat smoke and run real `lattice codex verify` in solver-visible after build.
